results.company_response: OpenAI states that it triaged the dozen-plus UK AISI vulnerability reports and made concrete changes: engineering product fixes, policy-enforcement implementation fixes, focused classifier training, robustness improvements to the monitoring stack measured against the universal jailbreaks UK AISI found, and product-configuration fixes closing the configuration vulnerabilities that allowed malicious content to be input or exfiltrated without triggering moderation. The pre-deployment system cards corroborate: the ChatGPT Agent system card records seven UK AISI universal attacks all patched, and the GPT-5 system card records a UK AISI jailbreak that evaded all mitigation layers being patched.
results.channel_a_verbatim: Some of these led to engineering based product fixes, some led to policy enforcement implementation fixes, and some led OpenAI to carry out focused training for improving certain aspects of our classifiers.

results.policy_response: In a Lords Grand Committee debate on the AI Regulation Bill on 2026-06-04, the DSIT/DBT Parliamentary Under-Secretary Baroness Lloyd of Effra told the House that AISI works closely with AI labs and that leading industry players including OpenAI have made changes to strengthen AI model safeguards on the basis of the institute's findings. A similar ministerial statement was made by Kanishka Narayan in the Commons AI Safety debate on 2025-12-10. The US NIST update of 2025-09-25 separately records that the OpenAI security improvements followed evaluations completed in partnership with the UK AI Security Institute. No binding instrument was located.

results.notes: Company-published finding: OpenAI's remediation appears in the same 2025-09-12 primary document as the finding, so Response Date = Publication Date and Lag = 0 (coordinated disclosure). Substantive is well supported: several distinct, specified and attributed changes (monitoring-stack robustness measured against the UK AISI universal jailbreaks, product-configuration fixes, policy-enforcement fixes, classifier retraining), corroborated by two pre-deployment company documents that are valid negative-lag sources under §8 (ChatGPT Agent system card 2025-07-17: seven UK AISI universal attacks all patched; GPT-5 system card 2025-08-07: a jailbreak evading all mitigation layers 'is being patched'). Channel A Verbatim is taken from the HTML post rather than the PDFs so that it is character-exact; the system-card sentences are described rather than quoted in the log because the extracted PDF text contains line breaks that would have to be repaired. Channel B caveat: both ministerial statements describe AISI findings driving OpenAI safeguard changes in general terms and neither names the September 2025 update or the specific vulnerability reports, and AISI sits within DSIT, the minister's own department; coded as non-binding uptake on the strength of the explicit OpenAI-plus-safeguards-plus-AISI-findings statement to Parliament, with the generality recorded here. Congressional record unsearched (congress.gov 403, govinfo API rate-limited).
